Stated Claim / Post Context:
Essential Caravans collapses - the latest in a long line of manufacturers closing across the industry

Essential Caravans, based in north Melbourne, entered voluntary administration last week, leaving hundreds of customers in the lurch.

Actual Article Body:
By ASHLEY NICKEL, NEWS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  00:48 AEDT, 28 October 2026   |  Updated:  03:25 AEDT, 28 October 2026

Another Australian caravan builder has collapsed with 200 workers left in the lurch.

Essential Caravans, based in north Melbourne, entered voluntary administration last week.

More than 20 caravan manufacturers, retailers and accessory suppliers have collapsed across Australia in 2025 and 2026.

Essential Caravans director Jamie Johnson has appointed Insolvency specialists Paul Allen and Glenn Franklin of PKF Melbourne as joint administrators, according to ASIC documents.

'The administrators and management team are conducting an immediate review of all current customer caravan builds and delivery schedules to minimise disruption to buyers and dealership partners,' they said in a statement.

'It is the intention that all current orders will be fulfilled.'

The administrators hoped to 'create a sustainable path forward for the Essential Caravans brand'.

It's understood part of the business's 'restructure' will include moving its manufacturing operations to a facility in Pakenham.

Essential Caravans, based in north Melbourne, entered voluntary administration last week

It was previously reported Essential was planning to shut its Somerton factory and transfer operations to Design RV's operation in Pakenham, of which Mr Johnson is also an owner.

Essential was registered with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) in 2015 by former directors Scott Grant, David Wilson and Ian Grant. Mr Johnson became director in 2020.

The company had built 5,000 caravans by March 2023 and was awarded a bronze honour in the Caravan Industry Association of Australia's People's Choice Manufacturer of the Year awards.

Nevertheless, the company couldn't escape the troubles plaguing the wider caravan industry in Australia.

Of the 20 major brands that have collapsed in recent years, many had major debts.

These include Australian Off Road which owes an estimated $14million and Maverick Campers with $6million.

Other brands to have gone into administration include Zone RV, Sunland RV, Network RV, Tango Caravans, Highline Caravans, Boss Adventure and Great Aussie Caravans.

Among the problems the industry is dealing with are cheaper imports, particularly from China, the rising cost of living putting luxuries off the table for many would-be buyers, and surging fuel costs making taking to the road prohibitively expensive.

Essential Caravans (above) joined the more than 20 caravan businesses to collapse in Australian in 2025 and 2026

Australian caravanning and camping YouTube channel Off Track urged their viewers to be careful when choosing a manufacturer so they don't get stung.

Hosts Ash and Dylan shared a list of 'red flags' that could precede a company's collapse.

'The first one is if they're asking for a huge deposit. Second is the phone suddenly stops getting answered,' they said.

'Warranty claims blowing out from weeks into months. Staff are constantly leaving.

'Social media accounts start to go quiet. Every second post on their socials is either a massive sale, factory cleanout, whatever.

'Delivery dates are getting pushed back. Facebook groups suddenly changing from people showing off their new vans to people asking have they received their vans yet or has anyone had a warranty approved.'

The pair added that while the red flags 'don't mean they're going bankrupt', they are repeated warning signs.

Additionally, they recommended checking prospective manufacturers on the ASIC company search to see if they've entered administration and Australian Business Number (ABN) search to ensure the business titles match government records.

The Daily Mail has contacted Essential Caravans for comment.

Should caravan buyers trust Aussie manufacturers or are imports a safer bet given all these collapses?
